text:
morgan: Hey team - noticed the curl example in the onboarding runbook returns a 404 when you hit the fragment anchor. thought it was a quick edit but want to confirm owner before I open a PR.

morgan: Repro: go to https://kb.redwood.ai/getting-started#quick-install then click the curl snippet. landing goes to /getting-started instead, the #quick-install anchor is missing.

alex: :eyes: can you paste the exact snippet? I'll try locally.

morgan: Sure—it's the inline example under 'Install & Run':

```bash
curl -sSL https://kb.redwood.ai/getting-started#quick-install | bash
```

morgan: That URL is probably fine but the page recently moved sections. I think the anchor id changed to `#install-cli`.

jen: I made a tiny restructure yesterday, sorry — I renamed the heading to match the CLI text. I can either revert or add a redirect/anchor. Which is preferred?

alex: If it's trivial, add a small HTML anchor or restore the heading slug. Otherwise update the snippet to point to #install-cli. Both fine, but need an owner to do the PR and CR.

sophie: I can take the PR and pair-review it. cc @jen — if you want to push the change I can review fast.

jen: I'll open a small PR to add an explicit anchor and update the snippet. will target the docs staging branch.

morgan: thanks! can you include a short changelog line so the docs-ship bot picks it up? e.g., `docs: fix onboarding curl anchor`

jen: yup. will do. pinging docs-bot to run the link-checker after merge.

docs-bot: scheduled link-checker job queued for 6321010400, will report results in #docs once done.

alex: one more ask — can we also add a tiny unit for the snippet in the docs tests so this doesn't regress? a single test that fetches the page and ensures the anchor exists.

jen: good call. adding that to the PR.

morgan: awesome. thanks everyone :tada: If anything blocks, drop it here and i'll help with the cr or tests.
